questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural savings digital = lu vo to
rural growth banking = ka mi vo
savings growth credit = ze mi lu
digital banking credit = to ze ka
rural savings credit = ze vo lu
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ze. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = vo, savings = lu, digital = to, growth = mi, banking = ka, credit = ze.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 40 km west, turns left and walks 60 km, then turns left and walks 15 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 65. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 25 km along the initial direction and 60 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(25² + 60²) = 65 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 106 km north, turns left and walks 180 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 204. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 96 km along the initial direction and 180 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(96² + 180²) = 204 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 29 km east, turns left and walks 36 km, then turns left and walks 14 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 15 km along the initial direction and 36 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(15² + 36²) = 39 km.

questions.stem: F is the mother of D. H is the daughter of D. E is the father of D. How is H related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. E is a parent of D, and H is D’s daughter. Hence H is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of A. A is the mother of H. E is the father of G and A. How is G related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of H’s mother A. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of B. B is the father of H. E is the son of H. A is the sister of B. How is B related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. B is the father of H, and H is E’s mother. Thus B is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 58 candidates, a candidate is 11th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. New front rank = 11+3 = 14. Back rank = 58 − 14 + 1 = 45.

questions.stem: In a queue of 38 candidates, a candidate is 11th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 24. New front rank = 11+4 = 15. Back rank = 38 − 15 + 1 = 24.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2400 each. One earns 20% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4666.67. Recover each cost separately: 2400×100/120 + 2400×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 58 and 87 hours. An outlet empties it in 116 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 49.71. Net rate = 1/58 + 1/87 − 1/116 = 7/348 tank/hour. Required time = 49.71 hours.

questions.stem: A boat covers 112 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. Still-water speed = 14 km/h. Upstream speed = 14 − 4. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 9:3. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 4 months. A receives ₹237600 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 264000. Profit ratio is 108:12. Each ratio unit = ₹2200. Total = 120 × 2200.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹29000 earns ₹17400 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 41760. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 20%. Compound amount = 29000 × (1 + 20/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 170 litres of pure milk. 34 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 108.8. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 170 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 23 people is 58 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 82. New total minus old total = (23+1)×(58+1) − 23×58 = 82.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 17 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+17)/(x+17) = 3/2 gives x = 17. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 290 m train moving at 93.6 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 7.2 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 12.08. Relative speed = (93.6 − 7.2) ×5/18 = 24 m/s. Time = 290/24.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3400. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.
